observations: body (figure): the figure is redrawn from the print: the circle about F through B and D, the circle about E, the eccentric about F, the epicycles about A, M and P and the ten straight lines, measured on the scan; the letters stand where they print.
body L1-L16: the sixteen lines beside the figure stand 14.1 pt apart on the scan, the lines below it 13.97 pt; each line is set at its printed place.
body L1, L20, L25, L29, L38: heavy brackets open and close Schiaparelli's additions; the addition begun in L38 goes on to p. 225.

body L1, L19, L31-L33, L37-L38: the dashes of «52–54», «13–18», «434–471» and «18–20» are long dashes (5.3 to 5.5 pt), as are those of «al–Battānī» (L19, L38), «’l–Wefā’» (L31), «’l–Wéfa» and «al–Bûzdjâni» (L32), 5.4 to 5.5 pt.

body L9, L20, L21, L29, L37: the dashes before «Quid» and before «Schiaparelli» (L20, L29) and after «b)» and «c)» in the heads measure 10.0 to 10.8 pt and are transcribed as dashes, as is that between «36» and «pag.» (10.1 pt).
body L27, L29: 6° 20′ 1/2 is the mean of 5° 1′ and 7° 40′; 6° 18′ less and more 1° 16′ gives the 5° 2′ and 7° 34′ of the moderns, as printed.
body L31: 1 Muḥarram 388 of the arithmetical calendar, counted from 15 July 622, is 2 January 998 (Julian), as printed.
body L35: the bars between ☾ and ⊙ and before m (9.7 to 10.2 pt) are minus signs. 1° 19′ 30″ is half of 7° 40′ − 5° 1′ = 2° 39′.

body L35-L36: in the variables of note 1, Ptolemy's lunar model (Almagest V: eccentric of radius 49p 41′, eccentricity 10p 19′, epicycle of 5p 15′, the mean apogee of the epicycle directed from the point opposite the centre of the eccentric) has no term in sin 2 (☾ − ⊙) alone: at a fixed elongation, as m runs once round, the Moon runs uniformly round the epicycle, which is symmetric about the line from the Earth to its centre, so the equation averages to zero; the rule of the tables, whose equations change sign with the corrected anomaly, has the same symmetry. Expanded numerically, the model gives terms of 6° 10′,6 in sin m and 1° 19′,6 in sin (2 [☾ − ⊙] − m), then 19′,9 in sin 2m and 17′,3 in sin (4 [☾ − ⊙] − m); the term 18′ sin 2 (☾ − ⊙) does not occur in these variables.

body L39: 60′ × 1° 53′ : 2° 40′ = 42′ 22″ 30‴; the 42′ 38″ of p. 53, l. 17 answer to the divisor 2° 39′ (60′ × 1° 53′ : 2° 39′ = 42′ 38″ 29‴), the value that the words of p. 53, l. 19–20 return; l. 16 there has 2° 2/3.
